newsitem.title: BELGIUM: One million could die in Zaire, EU says.
newsitem.headline: One million could die in Zaire, EU says.

text.p: One million people could die in Zaire, Emma Bonino, the European Union's humanitarian aid commissioner, said on Tuesday in calling for swift action from a world she accused of standing aloof from the unfolding tragedy.

"For the moment, 500,000 people are missing, we don't know where," she told reporters. "With the return of barbarism -- they are firing on the Red Cross -- the lives of one million people are in danger."
In Geneva, the U.N. refugee agency said in Geneva about 600,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutus were cut off from foreign aid in eastern Zaire.

U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees spokeswoman Ruth Marshall also reported fresh fighting near the sprawling refugee camps on Rwanda's borders which could set off a new exodus from the spreading conflict between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge fighters.
Bonino said the world had looked on as international conventions intended to protect humanitarian aid workers and U.N. protected camps were brushed aside in the fighting in Zaire.
She urged the United Nations to protect its refugee camps.
"The basis of humanitarian law has been totally violated, without there being a rebellion by the United Nations and the world Community," she said.
"I wonder at what point they are going to act," she said.
Zaire has fallen into a state of emergency during fighting between Zairian troops and Tutsi rebels.
Zaire announced on Monday night it was suspending all commercial air links to the troubled region to try to contain ethnic warfare.
Bonino said the closure of Goma airport by Zaire had made it impossible to restock with humanitarian aid.
Rwanda insisted on Monday it was not involved in clashes in eastern Zaire and called on Zaire not to expell ethnic tutsis who have always lived in the country and should be considered its nationals.
The Rwandan government, in a statement issued by its embassy in Brussels, urged Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire not to get involved in violence there and instead return home.
The U.N. fears the conflict could spread with the help of Tutsi domination armies in Burundi and Rwanda.
